answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a bonded stake with a slashing cliff. Each agent identity must lock collateral in the registry, and rewards unlock only after a long vesting ledge of many epochs. Faking ten thousand identities costs ten thousand deposits rather than cheap keypairs, and a fake cluster that farms payouts then abandons the vine loses its stake instead of a small fee. Because that stake is scored alongside real work records, attackers also pay ongoing compute to look genuine on the reef of task history. The economic barrier, not gatekeeping, makes mass identity ruinous.
